jiamingshi-jsphys/chelate-shell.html:
Chelate Shell

The missing orchestrator for your local agent skills. Orchestrating scattered local skills into a deterministic research and engineering workflow.

English · 简体中文

Version: 1.1.2 | Core Skills: 14 | Layers: 4 (workspace / ingest / gates / processors)

Security & Open Source Statement

Disclaimer: This repository contains auxiliary tools developed by the author to automate research workflows. It is not a peer-reviewed academic project. Some boilerplate or utility scripts may have been generated with the assistance of AI, and have been integrated with high-level review and modifications by the author. The author assumes no responsibility for any third-party code issues, but commits to promptly addressing any valid claims.

This tool will never do the experiment for you. Data must be collected manually by students in the lab; AI is absolutely physically isolated during the in-lab stage. Generated reports are merely "data-analysis drafts", and final academic responsibility lies with the user and their institution.

Why Chelate Shell?

In the current AI ecosystem, individual skills excel at solving isolated problems: validating formulas, tracking videos, or organizing files. However, when an Agent faces a complex task, it often struggles to determine which skill to invoke, in what order, and where to place the outputs.

Chelate Shell is an Orchestrator. It does not write low-level code to solve domain-specific problems. Instead, acting like a senior project manager, it decomposes user intents, enforces a standardized workspace directory structure, and deterministically routes tasks to the appropriate skills.

v1.1.0 Architecture: physical flatness + adapter isolation + microkernel

All 14 skills live flat under skills/ — no nested category folders — so AI platforms that scan a single directory level see every skill. Logical layering lives in each skill's manifest.json, and a tiny microkernel (core/) reads those manifests to build the pipeline.

chelate/
├── .claude-plugin/            # Claude Code plugin manifest + marketplace
├── .codebuddy-plugin/         # CodeBuddy plugin manifest + marketplace
├── .codex-plugin/             # Codex plugin manifest + marketplace
├── .dsh-plugin/               # DeepSeek Harness CJS entry (apply(ctx))
├── assets/                    # icon.png (shared by the plugin manifests)
├── index.js                   # CJS plugin entry (dsh ecosystem)
├── package.json               # npm/dsh packaging metadata
├── cordis.patch.yml           # cordis bundle patch
├── ORCHESTRATOR.md            # agent-facing routing contract (v1.1.0)
├── core/                      # microkernel
│   ├── router.py                # dispatcher: manifest-driven pipeline
│   ├── registry.py              # scans skills/ into a routing table
│   └── sandbox.py               # dependency resolution / degradation
├── contracts/                   # global contracts
│   ├── gate_result.py           # {skill, status, evidence_level, reason, artifacts}
│   └── schema.json              # manifest.json validation spec
├── lib/chelate_core/            # shared core library (logic lives here)
│   ├── adapter.py               # thin-adapter toolkit: argparse, gate emission, legacy runner
│   ├── paths.py / yamlmini.py   # path resolution / assets/config.yaml loading
│   ├── pdf_text.py              # PDF extraction core (pdfminer.six / pypdf)
│   ├── arxiv_search.py          # arXiv search core
│   ├── bibtex_norm.py           # BibTeX parse / dedupe / normalize core
│   ├── doi_audit.py             # DOI extraction + Crossref verification core
│   ├── csv_profile.py           # CSV profiling core (pandas)
│   └── formula_merge.py         # legacy D1-D5 + pint verdict merge policy
├── skills/                      # 14 skills, completely flat
│   ├── task-organizer/          #   workspace  (infrastructure)
│   ├── multi-dim-manager/       #   workspace  (infrastructure)
│   ├── document-evolution-tracker/ # workspace (infrastructure)
│   ├── capstone-labmate/        #   ingest     (extraction)
│   ├── video-tracker/           #   ingest     (extraction)
│   ├── fulltext-extractor/      #   ingest     (extraction, new)
│   ├── literature-retriever/    #   ingest     (extraction, new)
│   ├── bibtex-normalizer/       #   ingest     (extraction, new)
│   ├── formula-validator/       #   gates
│   ├── longitudinal-analysis/   #   gates
│   ├── conflict-detector/       #   gates
│   ├── reference-auditor/       #   gates      (new)
│   ├── data-profiler/           #   gates      (new)
│   └── ai-trace-remover/        #   processors
│       ├── SKILL.md             #   instructions for the AI platform
│       ├── manifest.json        #   metadata for the Router
│       ├── README.md            #   human-facing documentation
│       ├── LICENSE              #   MIT (per-skill copy)
│       ├── run.py               #   thin adapter: CLI wiring only
│       └── assets/              #   config.yaml and other dead resources
└── tests/                       # automated test suite (156 tests)

Every skill directory carries the same surface: SKILL.md for the AI, manifest.json for the Router, README.md for humans, LICENSE, and run.py — a thin adapter that only parses arguments and formats the gate result.

Installation

This repository is a cross-platform agent skill suite. Choose the installation method that fits you best.

Option 1: Install via Git link (recommended, agent-native)

  1. Open your platform's plugin manager (or marketplace configuration) UI.
  2. Choose "Install from Git repository" or "Add custom marketplace".
  3. Enter the repository URL and confirm: https://github.com/JiamingShi-JsPhys/chelate-shell

Option 2: Let your AI install it

Copy the following prompt to your AI Agent; it will clone the repository and configure it automatically:

"Please visit the GitHub repository https://github.com/JiamingShi-JsPhys/chelate-shell, clone it, and register all skills under the skills/ directory with your system according to the current agent platform's conventions."

Warning: When using AI auto-install, the AI will very likely break apart the standalone skills under skills/ and copy them flat into the platform's global skills directory. This disables Chelate Shell's microkernel auto-orchestration architecture and degrades it to 14 loose skills. If you need the full plugin orchestration functionality, use Option 1.

Environment dependencies: The microkernel and most skills depend only on the Python standard library. A few data/network-related skills require third-party libraries (see the dependency matrix below). When a dependency is missing, the system degrades gracefully to an UNVERIFIED gate with a hint instead of crashing.

Debugging

One switch, every layer: add --debug to any cli.py subcommand (list / run / pipeline) or to core/router.py, or export CHELATE_DEBUG=1 for the whole process tree. The flag sets the same environment variable, so skill subprocesses inherit it automatically.

# debug one skill directly (flag may sit before or after the skill name)
python cli.py run data-profiler --root /path/to/workspace --action profile --input data.csv --debug

# debug a whole pipeline
CHELATE_DEBUG=1 python cli.py pipeline --root /path/to/workspace --mode c --selected reference-auditor

With the switch on, stderr receives [chelate:debug] lines covering the registry scan, the resolved subprocess command and cwd, the dependency verdict (degraded / missing), the return code and duration, the last stderr lines of each skill, the legacy action → module mapping, and the final gate path with its status. stdout is never polluted — the single gate-contract JSON line stays machine-parseable. Output colors follow NO_COLOR / CHELATE_FORCE_COLOR.

For post-mortem analysis, every run leaves machine-readable traces: process/gates/<skill>_<ts>.json (one gate result per skill), results/pipeline_report_<ts>.json (the full decision record, including the command, degraded flag, missing dependencies, return code and seconds of every skill), and _broadcast/pipeline_index_<ts>.json (the compact context-compression index).

Quick start

# list the 14 registered skills
python cli.py list

# run one skill directly
python cli.py run reference-auditor --root /path/to/workspace \
    --action audit --input draft.md

# dry-run a pipeline (shows the planned execution order)
python cli.py pipeline --root /path/to/workspace --mode a --input-kind pdf --dry-run

# full pipeline: ingest -> gates -> processors
python cli.py pipeline --root /path/to/workspace --mode a --input-kind pdf

# gates only, with per-skill arguments
python cli.py pipeline --root /path/to/workspace --mode c \
    --selected reference-auditor \
    --skill-arg "reference-auditor:--input draft.md"

# declare the run's input files: each is wired as --input to the plan
# skills whose manifest input_types declare its type (missing files fail
# fast with exit code 2 before anything runs)
python cli.py pipeline --root ./test_workspace --inputs draft.md data.csv

Pipeline modes: a auto (ingest → gates → processors), b extract-only, c gates-only. --inputs narrows the plan to the skills that can consume the declared files (an explicit --selected list always wins); a file whose extension declares no manifest type is reported as an [INPUT] warning and wires to nothing.

The 14 skills

Workspace (infrastructure)

  • task-organizer — four-zone workspace init, file organization (C1–C8 validation, dedupe, snapshots, undo/redo), _broadcast/INDEX.md context index
  • multi-dim-manager — parameter-space expansion, SHA-256 snapshots, hash audit logs, safe rollback to any past round
  • document-evolution-tracker — paragraph-level diff across document versions with concept-lineage tracking

Ingest (extraction)

  • capstone-labmate — PASCO Capstone .cap binary parsing, CSV/JSON conversion, watermarked draft reports
  • video-tracker — OpenCV coordinate extraction (CSRT/Template trackers), FFT spectrum analysis, physics consistency probes
  • fulltext-extractor (new) — pdfminer.six text extraction into process/ (pypdf fallback)
  • literature-retriever (new) — arXiv keyword search to JSON
  • bibtex-normalizer (new) — .bib parsing, dedupe, normalized output

Gates

  • formula-validator — SymPy D1–D5 layers (dimensional analysis, limit enumeration, numeric sampling, symbolic proof) merged with a pint physical-unit cross-check
  • longitudinal-analysis — time-series OLS plus R-backed LMM (lme4), mediation (lavaan) and sensitivity analysis; degrades to pure-Python steps when Rscript is absent
  • conflict-detector — cross-document contradiction engine with regex number extraction for hard cross-checks
  • reference-auditor (new) — DOI extraction and Crossref verification; a non-existent DOI fails the gate
  • data-profiler (new) — pandas CSV profiling: row counts, missing-value statistics, 1.5·IQR outlier ratios, duplicates, constant columns

Processors

  • ai-trace-remover — template-sentence removal and a 0–100 "AI-likeness" score (clean-room English lexicon plus the full Chinese lexicon)

Migration guarantee (v1.0.0 → v1.1.0)

The nine legacy skills were migrated byte-for-byte: 179 Python files (~37,400 lines) plus all non-code assets were copied with SHA-256 verification, and the internal package layout (scripts.*, src.*, R/, templates/, config/) is unchanged. The only additions are each skill's root run.py adapter, its manifest.json, and — for formula-validator — a new scripts/core/pint_units.py layer. A guard test (tests/test_capability_guard.py) re-verifies file parity and the presence of every key module function on every run.

Tests

python -m pytest tests/ -q     # 156 tests

The suite covers the gate contract, manifest schema validation, flat-layout enforcement, pipeline planning and FAIL termination, the migration guard, the legacy D1–D5 and FFT/physics probes, the five new skills, workspace input-path resolution, --inputs auto-wiring (manifest-type matching, plan narrowing, fail-fast on missing files), the unified debug layer (switch semantics plus a real-subprocess integration test for the router's debug plumbing), and the manifest-contract suite (plugin manifests for all four host platforms: author-object, no string skills, no icon, version sync; SKILL.md frontmatter agreeing with each manifest).

Requirements

Python 3.10+. Per-skill dependencies are declared in each manifest.json and resolved at run time by core/sandbox.py; a missing dependency degrades the skill to an UNVERIFIED gate instead of crashing the pipeline.

Third-party packages are used at run time only; none are vendored into this repository, and each remains under its own license (e.g. numpy/pandas BSD, OpenCV Apache-2.0, SymPy/pint/requests/bibtexparser/arxiv BSD/MIT/Apache, pdfminer. six is MIT; pypdf is BSD-3-Clause — both permissive). Optional dependencies are imported behind try/ImportError or action-scoped conditionals, so a missing one degrades that feature (or that config format) — never the whole skill.

It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by PASCO Scientific. All .cap parsing runs locally; users are responsible for complying with their institution's academic-integrity policy.

jiamingshi-jsphys/chem-notes.html:
English | 简体中文

General Chemistry — Notes

This project contains lecture notes on general chemistry, written with the reusable chemistry.cls document class and typeset in LaTeX. Both English and Chinese versions are provided.

Author: Jiaming Shi, Department of Physics, Westlake University.

Compiled PDFs

The latest compiled PDFs are available on the Releases page:

  • General_Chemistry_en.pdf
  • General_Chemistry_zh.pdf

Or visit the latest Releases.

Compilation

Main documents:

General_Chemistry_en.tex
General_Chemistry_zh.tex

Compile the English version:

latexmk -xelatex -interaction=nonstopmode -file-line-error \
  -output-directory=build General_Chemistry_en.tex

To compile the Chinese version, replace the filename with General_Chemistry_zh.tex. All build artifacts are written to build/.

The Chinese version uses the chinese class option:

\documentclass[chinese]{chemistry}

This loads ctexart and switches environment names to Chinese. The English version uses:

\documentclass{chemistry}

Directory Structure

chem-notes/
├── General_Chemistry_en.tex
├── General_Chemistry_zh.tex
├── chemistry.cls
├── chapters_en/
├── chapters_zh/
├── build/
├── README.md
└── README_zh.md
  • chemistry.cls: shared document class containing the page layout, packages, fonts, theorem boxes, and custom macros.
  • General_Chemistry_en.tex / General_Chemistry_zh.tex: entry points for the English / Chinese versions.
  • chapters_en/ / chapters_zh/: chapter source files for the English / Chinese versions.
  • build/: build artifacts, excluded from Git.

Current Status

Chapters 1–3 are complete; Chapters 4–7 are in progress. The shared preamble lives in chemistry.cls, and each chapter contains only \section-level content. To add notes, create a new file in chapters_en/ or chapters_zh/ and add an \input line to the corresponding main file.

Reporting Issues

If you find a typo, a wrong equation, or a build issue, please open an issue and include the subject, page/section, and the exact line.

  • Repository: JiamingShi-JsPhys/chem-notes
  • Issues: JiamingShi-JsPhys/chem-notes/issues

jietexue/quantum-mechanics-notes.html:
Quantum Mechanics Notes - Fall 2025

Personal study notes for the Fall 2025 Quantum Mechanics course at Westlake University, taught by Congjun Wu. The notes are written primarily in English using LaTeX.

Instructor's lecture notes: Quantum Mechanics 2025.

These notes do not follow the order of the lectures. Topics, derivations, and computational methods are reorganized around my own understanding, with a strongly personal approach to selection, presentation, and emphasis. They are not official lecture notes or a complete record of the course, and may contain errors or omissions.

Contents

  • Foundations: quantization, Dirac notation, operators, commutators, compatible observables, and uncertainty relations.
  • Wave functions and dynamics: position and momentum representations, the Schrodinger equation, probability density and current, exponential operators, and the Baker-Hausdorff lemma.
  • Model systems: analytical and algebraic treatments of the harmonic oscillator, coherent states, gauge transformations, Landau levels, and the quantum Hall effect.
  • Angular momentum and symmetries: rotations, spherical harmonics, angular momentum addition, Clebsch-Gordan coefficients, parity, and time reversal.
  • Approximation methods: time-independent and time-dependent perturbation theory, the interaction picture, the Landau-Zener model, adiabatic evolution, and the Berry phase.
  • Path integrals and scattering: propagators, Feynman's path integral formulation, and partial-wave scattering.

Build

The main source is quantum-mechanics-notes.tex; illustrations and their SVG source are in figures/.

With a TeX distribution containing the required packages and latexmk installed, run from the repository root:

latexmk -pdf quantum-mechanics-notes.tex

Overview / 概述

This repository contains the lecture notes for Calculus Track A (both semesters), delivered by Prof. Yabin Zhang (张雅彬) at the 2025 academic year. The notes have been compiled and uploaded with the explicit permission of the instructor.

本仓库为 2025 学年微积分 A 类（上、下）课程讲义，由 张雅彬 老师授课。讲义经授课教师明确同意后整理上传。

Textbook and References / 教材与参考资料

  • Primary Textbook / 主要教材
    Tom M. Apostol, Calculus, Volume I (2nd edition) and Calculus, Volume II (2nd edition).
    本课程以 Tom M. Apostol 所著《Calculus》第一卷与第二卷（第二版）为主要教材。

Who Should Use These Notes / 适用人群

  • Pre-study / 课前预习
    If you have not yet taken the course and wish to prepare in advance, these notes can serve as a structured preview of the material and its scope.
    若您尚未修读本课程并希望提前预习，本讲义可作为课程内容与范围的结构化预览。

  • Review / 课后复习
    If you have already taken the course and wish to consolidate your understanding or revisit specific topics, these notes provide a reorganized and annotated reference.
    若您已修读本课程，希望巩固理解或回顾特定知识点，本讲义可作为经过重排与注解的参考资料。

  • Exam Scope Reference (Credit Exemption) / 免修考试范围参考
    If you have previously self-studied calculus and intend to sit for a credit exemption exam, these notes can help you gauge the breadth and depth of the course coverage. However, please note that the exam syllabus may vary slightly from year to year.
    若您已自学过微积分并希望参加免修考试，本讲义可帮助您了解课程的覆盖范围与深度。但请注意，每年考纲可能略有变动。

Who Should NOT Use These Notes / 不适用人群

  • First-Time Self-Learners / 首次自学微积分者
    These notes were not designed as a standalone textbook. They assume the presence of an instructor and are intended to complement, rather than replace, classroom instruction. Readers encountering calculus for the first time are strongly advised to use a comprehensive textbook alongside these materials.
    本讲义并非为独立学习而设计。讲义假定读者有授课教师指导，旨在补充而非替代课堂教学。强烈建议首次接触微积分的读者在参考本讲义的同时，系统使用一本完整的教材。

How These Notes Were Created / 讲义的创作过程

These notes were compiled through the following process:

  1. Board note transcription / 板书整理 — The core content is based on Prof. Zhang's lecture board work. It has been reorganized and typeset, with some statements rephrased in equivalent form and supplemented by minor explanatory adjustments where appropriate.
  2. Motivational context and remarks / 动机阐释与评注 — The author has added their own commentary to provide motivation, intuitive explanations, and supplementary remarks where deemed helpful.
  3. Restructuring and pruning / 重排与删节 — The material has undergone a degree of rearrangement to improve logical flow, and overly trivial examples have been removed to keep the notes concise.
  4. Supplementary content / 补充内容 — Material from exercise sessions (习题课) and homework assignments has been incorporated to enrich the treatment of certain topics.

In summary, these notes are not a verbatim transcript of lectures; they are a curated and augmented version, shaped by the author's own perspective on the subject.

本讲义的创作过程如下：

  1. 板书整理 — 核心内容基于张老师的课堂板书整理而成。笔记在整理与排版过程中对部分表述进行了等价改写，并在适当位置加入了少量解释性补充;
  2. 动机阐释与评注 — 作者适当加入了自身的理解与评注，以提供学习动机和直观解释；
  3. 重排与删节 — 对内容进行了一定程度的重排以优化逻辑脉络，并删去了部分过于简单的例题；
  4. 补充内容 — 结合习题课与课后作业内容，对相关知识点进行了补充。

Disclaimer / 注意事项

These notes may contain typographical or mathematical errors. If you spot any, please feel free to open an issue in this repository. Contributions and corrections are welcome.

本讲义可能存在排版错误或数学笔误。如您发现任何问题，欢迎在本仓库提交 Issue。感谢您的反馈与指正。

License / 许可

The lecture content is based on Prof. Yabin Zhang's lectures and is shared with the instructor's consent. Please do not redistribute these notes for commercial purposes without permission.

讲义内容基于张雅彬老师的授课内容，已获得授课教师的分享许可。请勿在未经许可的情况下将这些笔记用于商业目的。

    若您已自学过线性代数并希望参加免修考试，本讲义可帮助您了解课程的覆盖范围与深度。但请注意，每年考纲可能略有变动。

Who Should NOT Use These Notes / 不适用人群

  • First-Time Self-Learners / 首次自学线性代数者
    These notes were not designed as a standalone textbook. They assume the presence of an instructor and are intended to complement, rather than replace, classroom instruction. Readers encountering linear algebra for the first time are strongly advised to use a comprehensive textbook alongside these materials.
    本讲义并非为独立学习而设计。讲义假定读者有授课教师指导，旨在补充而非替代课堂教学。强烈建议首次接触线性代数的读者在参考本讲义的同时，系统使用一本完整的教材。

How These Notes Were Created / 讲义的创作过程

These notes were compiled through the following process:

  1. Board note transcription / 板书整理 — The core content is based on Prof. Zhang's lecture board work. It has been reorganized and typeset, with some statements rephrased in equivalent form and supplemented by minor explanatory adjustments where appropriate.
  2. Motivational context and remarks / 动机阐释与评注 — The author has added their own commentary to provide motivation, intuitive explanations, and supplementary remarks where deemed helpful.
  3. Restructuring and pruning / 重排与删节 — The material has undergone a degree of rearrangement to improve logical flow, and overly trivial examples have been removed to keep the notes concise.
  4. Supplementary content / 补充内容 — Material from exercise sessions (习题课) and homework assignments has been incorporated to enrich the treatment of certain topics.

In summary, these notes are not a verbatim transcript of lectures; they are a curated and augmented version, shaped by the author's own perspective on the subject.

本讲义的创作过程如下：

  1. 板书整理 — 核心内容基于张老师的课堂板书整理而成。笔记在整理与排版过程中对部分表述进行了等价改写，并在适当位置加入了少量解释性补充;
  2. 动机阐释与评注 — 作者适当加入了自身的理解与评注，以提供学习动机和直观解释；
  3. 重排与删节 — 对内容进行了一定程度的重排以优化逻辑脉络，并删去了部分过于简单的例题；
  4. 补充内容 — 结合习题课与课后作业内容，对相关知识点进行了补充。

Disclaimer / 注意事项

These notes may contain typographical or mathematical errors. If you spot any, please feel free to open an issue in this repository. Contributions and corrections are welcome.

Fundamental Algebra and Analysis

This repository archives the source files for the Fundamental Algebra and Analysis course notes.

Course edition: 2025 Fall–2026 Spring (2025fall, 2026spring). Repository: FAA-lecture-notes-2025fall-2026spring.

As of June 24, 2026, all course sessions have ended. The repository is kept mainly as an archive of the LaTeX sources for the two parts of the course:

  • faa-notes.cls: shared document class, based on book
  • part-1.tex, part-2.tex: entry points for the two lecture-note volumes
  • part-1/chapters/, part-2/chapters/: chapter sources
  • part-1/thinking-and-method.tex: supplementary notes
  • release-notes.md: release description draft

Compiled PDFs, including exercises and other handouts when available, will be packaged and published through GitHub Releases. Please check the repository's Releases page for downloadable PDF bundles instead of expecting built PDFs to be committed directly to the source tree.

Maintenance will be very infrequent. Future updates are expected only when someone reports a typo, correction, or small improvement and contributes it directly.

Building

Use a full TeX Live or MacTeX installation with XeLaTeX and latexmk. From the repository root, run:

latexmk -xelatex -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error part-1.tex
latexmk -xelatex -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error part-2.tex
latexmk -cd -xelatex -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error part-1/thinking-and-method.tex

The included .latexmkrc compiles with XeLaTeX in the source directory, keeps working files (including .aux, .log, .xdv, and SyncTeX) in the repository's build/ directory, and copies only the final PDF beside its .tex source:

part-1.tex                 -> part-1.pdf
part-2.tex                 -> part-2.pdf
part-1/thinking-and-method.tex -> part-1/thinking-and-method.pdf

build/ also retains working copies of the PDFs for incremental compilation. Do not pass -outdir or -auxdir, which override this configuration. Build Part I before the supplementary notes, which read its .aux files from build/ and link to part-1.pdf. PDFs and the entire build/ directory are ignored by Git. After changing or deleting a published PDF, run the corresponding build command again to refresh it.

VS Code user-level recipes can apply the same layout globally using a build/ directory beside each document entry point; the PDF preview and SyncTeX can use the working PDF there while the published PDF stays beside the source.

The lecture notes use \documentclass[part-one]{faa-notes} or \documentclass[part-two]{faa-notes}. The latter preserves Part II's extra mathematical operators, list packages, number-first theorem headings, and shared axiom counter. Standard book options, such as oneside, are forwarded. Existing mathematical commands and environment names remain compatible. Source paths use lowercase ASCII names with hyphens and two-digit chapter numbers; standard repository files such as README.md and LICENSE retain their names.

Contributing

Typo fixes and small corrections are welcome. If you notice an error, please open an issue or submit a pull request with a focused change.

这个仓库用于归档 代数与分析基础 课程讲义的源文件。

截至 2026 年 6 月 24 日，今天所有课程均已结束。本仓库主要作为两部分课程 LaTeX 源文件的归档：

编译后的 PDF，包括习题和其他讲义材料（如有），会打包发布在 GitHub Releases 中。请优先在本仓库的 Releases 页面下载 PDF 包，而不是期待编译后的 PDF 被直接提交到源代码目录中。

之后本仓库的维护频率会非常低。预计只有在有人主动指出 typo、修正错误，或贡献小改进时，才会继续更新。

编译

安装包含 XeLaTeX 和 latexmk 的完整 TeX Live 或 MacTeX，在仓库根目录运行上方命令。 仓库内的 .latexmkrc 会将 .aux、.log、.xdv、SyncTeX 等工作文件统一放到 根目录的 build/，仅将最终 PDF 复制到对应 .tex 的同级目录，具体位置见上方示例。 build/ 中也会保留用于增量编译的 PDF 工作副本。不要额外传入 -outdir 或 -auxdir，以免覆盖该配置。 补充笔记会读取 build/ 中第一部分的 .aux 文件并链接到 part-1.pdf， 因此需先编译 part-1.tex。PDF 和整个 build/ 不会提交到 Git。 若修改或删除了同级目录的 PDF，重新运行相应编译命令即可更新。 VS Code 全局编译配方也可采用相同布局，在各编译入口旁的 build/ 中保存工作文件； 预览和 SyncTeX 使用其中的 PDF 工作副本，同级目录保留最终 PDF。

两部分分别使用 \documentclass[part-one]{faa-notes} 和 \documentclass[part-two]{faa-notes}。第二部分保留原有的附加数学命令、 列表宏包、编号在前的定理标题及共享的公理计数器，oneside 等标准 book 选项会传递给基础类。正文中已有的数学命令和环境名保持兼容。 源码路径统一使用小写英文、连字符和两位章节编号，README.md、LICENSE 等标准仓库文件名保留。

贡献

欢迎提交 typo 修正和小范围勘误。如果你发现问题，可以开 issue，或者直接提交一个聚焦的 pull request。

本仓库采用 MIT License 发布。详情见 LICENSE。
